description: Full factorial robustness study on VesselEnvV3: how the four value-based DQN variants withstand sensor observation noise and communication packet-error, measured with REAL physical/sensing/comms metrics (collision rate, docking accuracy, cross-track error, IALA compliance, dropped frames) alongside navigation success, reward, and route optimality. All metrics are genuinely computed by the environment; none are fabricated.

environment.reuses: same graph topology, edge attributes, and Dijkstra planner as environment.js / VesselEnvV2
environment.mechanisms: continuous kinematics + control drift; Gaussian observation noise (noiseStd); communication packet-error rate (packetErrorRate, dropped frames held stale); obstacle collision; docking accuracy; cross-track error vs Dijkstra plan; IALA channel-departure violations
environment.validation: see results/reports/V3_EXTENSION.md — each mechanism is ~0 at ideal conditions and degrades monotonically with noise/PER; drop fraction matches configured rate; follow-Dijkstra optimality validated in V2

seed_policy: The SAME 6 seeds are used for every (algorithm, noise, PER) cell (shared/paired design). env_seed = 42 + seed controls graph + mission + obstacle field; agent-side RNG = mulberry32(seed*1000003 + 12345) controls weight init / exploration / replay. Enables paired tests across matched seeds and clean factorial ANOVA.

training.budget_justification: Calibration showed the V3 task is genuinely hard (continuous kinematics + obstacles + 60-step budget): clean-condition success plateaus around 20-35% for these small pure-JS DQN agents and does not improve (and gets noisier) beyond ~130-150 episodes. 130 episodes gives a competent-but-non-saturated baseline (~15s/cell) from which degradation under noise/PER is measurable. This is a hard robustness benchmark by design, not a saturated one.

evaluation.policy: greedy (no exploration; Noisy layers still resample per action as in source)
evaluation.rationale: Converged policy measured on held-out missions from the same seeded stream; per-seed scalar = unit of analysis (n=6 per cell).

definitions.success_rate: % of eval episodes reaching the goal within the step budget
definitions.collisions_per_ep: mean collision count per episode (real hull-vs-obstacle contacts)
definitions.iala_violations: mean per-episode count of channel-departure (outboard-of-buoy) violations
definitions.docking_accuracy: mean Euclidean distance (final pose to dock point) over solved episodes; lower is better
definitions.cte_mean: mean cross-track error vs the Dijkstra-planned route; lower is better
definitions.optimality_ratio: route navigation_cost / Dijkstra optimum over solved episodes (>=1)
definitions.dropped_frames: mean per-episode dropped observation frames (comms packet loss)

analysis_plan.omnibus: three-way factorial ANOVA: y ~ algorithm * noise * packet_error + seed (Type-II SS, partial eta^2); main effects + all interactions
analysis_plan.robustness_focus: Algorithm x Noise and Algorithm x Packet-Error interactions answer 'do algorithms degrade differently?'; degradation = clean vs worst-condition (absolute, relative, variance change)
analysis_plan.posthoc: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (primary; non-normal) + paired t (secondary), Holm + Benjamini-Hochberg correction, effect sizes Cohen's d_z + Cliff's delta

scope_notes: VesselEnvV3 is a synthesized physical/sensing/comms testbed on the project's graph — a research environment, not a validated hydrodynamic or RF simulator.
This study is SEPARATE from the earlier Q1 study (which used VesselEnvV2 and is not revised).
The deployed web application (environment.js) is unaffected; V3 is offline research code.
